# fzf - a command-line fuzzy finder

fzf is a general-purpose command-line fuzzy finder.

It's an interactive filter program for any kind of list; files, command
history, processes, hostnames, bookmarks, git commits, etc. It implements
a "fuzzy" matching algorithm, so you can quickly type in patterns with omitted
characters and still get the results you want.

## Highlights

- **Portable** — Distributed as a single binary for easy installation
- **Fast** — Optimized to process millions of items instantly
- **Versatile** — Fully customizable through an event-action binding mechanism
- **All-inclusive** — Comes with integrations for Bash, Zsh, Fish, Vim, and Neovim

## Installation

fzf is available via multiple package managers:

### macOS

- Homebrew: `brew install fzf`
- MacPorts: `sudo port install fzf`

### Linux

- Alpine Linux: `sudo apk add fzf`
- Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install fzf`
- Fedora: `sudo dnf install fzf`
- Arch Linux: `sudo pacman -S fzf`
- And many more distributions

### Windows

- Chocolatey: `choco install fzf`
- Scoop: `scoop install fzf`
- Winget: `winget install fzf`

### Binary releases

You can download official fzf binaries from:
- https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/releases

## Usage

fzf is an interactive Unix filter program. It reads a list of items from
standard input, allows you to select a subset of the items, and prints the
selected ones to standard output.

### Basic Usage

```sh
# Find files
find * -type f | fzf

# Find processes
ps aux | fzf

# Find command history
history | fzf
```

### Display Modes

#### --height mode

Use `--height` option to limit the height of the finder:

```sh
fzf --height 40%
```

#### --tmux mode

fzf can be displayed in a tmux popup window:

```sh
fzf --tmux
```

### Search Syntax

Unless specified otherwise, fzf starts in "extended-search mode" where you can
type in multiple search terms delimited by spaces.

| Token     | Match type                 | Description                          |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `sbtrkt`  | fuzzy-match                | Items that match `sbtrkt`            |
| `'wild`   | exact-match (quoted)       | Items that include `wild`            |
| `^music`  | prefix-exact-match         | Items that start with `music`        |
| `.mp3$`   | suffix-exact-match         | Items that end with `.mp3`           |
| `!fire`   | inverse-exact-match        | Items that do not include `fire`     |
| `!^music` | inverse-prefix-exact-match | Items that do not start with `music` |
| `!.mp3$`  | inverse-suffix-exact-match | Items that do not end with `.mp3`    |

### Key Bindings

- `CTRL-J` / `CTRL-K` (or `CTRL-N` / `CTRL-P`) - Move cursor up and down
- `Enter` - Select the item
- `CTRL-C` / `CTRL-G` / `ESC` - Exit
- `Tab` - Mark multiple items
- `Shift-Tab` - Unmark items

### Common Options

- `-m, --multi` - Enable multi-select with Tab/Shift-Tab
- `-x, --extended` - Extended-search mode (enabled by default)
- `-e, --exact` - Enable exact-match
- `-i, --ignore-case` - Case-insensitive match
- `+i, --no-ignore-case` - Case-sensitive match
- `--height HEIGHT[%]` - Display height
- `--tmux [CENTER|TOP|BOTTOM|LEFT|RIGHT][,SIZE[%]]` - Display in tmux popup
- `--preview COMMAND` - Command to preview highlighted item
- `--bind KEY:ACTION` - Bind keys to custom actions
- `--color [BASE_SCHEME][,COLOR:ANSI]` - Color scheme

### Examples

```sh
# Find and open a file in your editor
vim $(fzf)

# Search command history
history | fzf

# Kill a process
ps aux | fzf | awk '{print $2}' | xargs kill

# Preview file contents
fzf --preview 'cat {}'

# Multi-select files
fzf --multi

# Custom height
fzf --height 40%
```

### Environment Variables

- `FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND` - Default command to use for listing items
- `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS` - Default options to fzf
- `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE` - Path to file containing default options

## Advanced Usage

For more advanced usage examples, see [ADVANCED.md](ADVANCED.md).

For Vim/Neovim plugin usage, see [README-VIM.md](README-VIM.md).

## Documentation

- Manual pages are available via `man fzf` and `man fzf-tmux`
- Vim documentation is available via `:help fzf`
